name: Burkitts Reef ("Greg's Reef"), Bargara, Queensland

confidence.reason: The outline is a photo trace of the visible basalt rock platform (the natural headland) on one dated satellite image. The reef itself is only the part of the platform whose boulders were moved in 1997, and no source says where that part is, so the drawing shows the stage the reef sits on, not the reef.
factors: Rock platform clearly visible on georeferenced Esri imagery (2025-09-05), outer edge follows the breaker line within about 10 m
Reshaped zone is not defined in any source (card: no footprint figure; Wikipedia: 'not a structure in and of itself')
Polygon is cut by the image frame on the south side (platform continues beyond the frame)
Single image, single date; no second image, no survey, no design drawing exists
Landward edge follows vegetation / sand boundary judged by eye (plus or minus about 5 m)

canonical.frame: metres; NOT a shoreline-aligned frame (the platform wraps round a curved headland, so no single alongshore axis exists): origin = polygon centroid, +x = east, +y = north (UTM 56S axes)
canonical.note: Frame deliberately N-up; distance offshore 0 m (attached headland, card/R1,R2,R10). Area is for the in-frame part only (south edge cut by the frame).

geo.method: pixel -> lat/lon by linear interpolation of the sidecar bounds in Web Mercator y and linear lon (scripts/compute_shape.py); area re-computed in UTM 56S and geodesically

angles.what: outer (seaward) edge of the east flank, vertices 12-21 of the trace, bearing of the line
angles.method: atan2 on pixel vertices (1230,920)->(1610,1991): 380 px east, 1071 px south; so the flank trends ~160/340 deg true and the seaward direction is ~70 deg true (ENE)
pixel vertices (760,675)->(1130,790): 370 px east, 115 px south

outline_versions.name: Visible rock platform, photo trace (Esri imagery 2025-09-05)
outline_versions.method: Polygon read by eye on the georeferenced image (full-resolution zoom grids), converted with the sidecar bounds.
outline_versions.level: outer limit of the dark basalt rock platform visible at the image time (rock awash or exposed; edge = breaker line); this is the natural headland that carries the reshaped boulder reef, not the reshaped zone itself
outline_versions.note: South edge cut by the image frame; real platform is larger. Low confidence.

versions_info: There is only one outline: a photo trace of the visible basalt rock platform on Esri World Imagery captured 5 Sep 2025. No survey or design drawing of this reef exists, so the photo trace is the default by necessity. The reef itself is just the part of this platform where boulders were moved in 1997, and no source says where that part is, so treat the outline as the natural headland on which the reef sits. It is cut off at the south edge of the image.
